history.dynasty: Vemulawada Chalukyas (750-973 CE, with Vemulawada as their capital); present temple built under the Kalyani Chalukyas (11th-12th centuries)
history.period: 11th-12th centuries - built by Rajadithya, a governor of the Kalyani Chalukyas; the region was ruled earlier by Ikshvakus and Satavahanas
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the 'Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Temple [Karimnagar]' is the famous Rajanna temple at VEMULAWADA - NOT Karimnagar town. It stands ~35 km from Karimnagar city (sources vary: 34/36/38/53 km - conflict flagged) in Rajanna Sircilla district (older sources say Karimnagar district, before bifurcation). Identity certainty: HIGH - the Vemulawada temple is THE Raja Rajeshwara shrine of the region. Built by Kalyani Chalukya governor Rajadithya in the 11th-12th centuries, it was once the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (750-973 CE; older names Lemulavatika, Lembulavade). It is known as 'Dakshina Kasi' and as a 'Harihara Kshetram' for its two Vaishnava shrines (Anantha Padmanabha and Seetharama Chandra) inside the Shiva complex. Legend: after Kashi, Chidambaram, Srisailam and Kedareswar, Shiva chose to reside here. Features: Dharma Gundam tank (holy bath with believed medicinal properties before darshan), Kode Mokku (pradakshinam of the temple with a bull, Nandi's vahanam), and a Muslim saint's dargah in the complex. Associated with 11th-century Telugu poet Vemulawada Bheemakavi and with Kannada poet Pampa (court poet of Arikesari II).

name: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Swamy Temple
town: Vemulawada (CSV town 'Karimnagar' is WRONG - the temple is at Vemulawada, ~35 km from Karimnagar city, in Rajanna Sircilla district)
town_description: Vemulawada is a temple town in Rajanna Sircilla district, Telangana, about 36 km from Karimnagar and 151 km from Hyderabad, on the Karimnagar-Kamareddy bus route and on the banks of the Mulavagu stream. Once the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas (750-973 CE), it is one of Telangana's most famous pilgrimage sites, with nearby attractions Agraharam Hanuman Temple, Baddi Pochamma Temple and Nampally Gutta.

travel.road: On the Karimnagar-Kamareddy bus route; frequent TSRTC buses from Warangal, Karimnagar, Secunderabad and Hyderabad (verify).
